posts.title: Interview: Encantada – Prefiero Ser Arte (November 2026)
posts.description: Amanda Muñoz Hüttl has a habit her mother spotted when she was a small child: whenever she liked what was on her plate, she started to sing, and she still does. Her mother always read the signal the same way: “Ok, Amanda is enjoying the food because she’s singing” . Years later, that habit and her love of the Spanish expression me encanta , with the verb cantar inside it, gave her solo project its name: Encantada . This weekend she plays Italy for the first time, with two house concerts in Matera and Taranto for Hauskonzerte , run by the Altamura-based association Xilema to promote independent music. Xilema’s other project, Migrasom , is a programme of meetings backed by the Puglia regional council’s gender-equality scheme, bringing artists, students and residents of Bari, Taranto and Lecce together to look at music, images and gender from an anthropological angle. posts.title: Daily Discovery: Doris Lavin – Cantar es Mi Vida
posts.description: “Cantar es Mi Vida” sets three generations of Cuban son singers over the chord cycle of “Guantanamera”, backed by the Septeto Nacional Ignacio Piñeiro , the Havana band that Ignacio Piñeiro founded in 1927. The single belongs to Doris Lavin , a son singer from Colón in Matanzas province who moved to Italy in 1996 and now lives in Switzerland. She wrote and produced it, recorded it in Havana at PM Records, the studio of Pablo Milanés , and released it herself on 8 November. Over that borrowed three-chord loop Lavin wrote six new coplas , short rhymed verses, and shared them with Daniel Vera , a Havana singer born in 1963 and schooled by the city’s old masters, and Lester Ciarreta Hernández , a younger Cuban singer based in Mexico who came up through salsa bands on the island. Lavin sings for the generation between them. Both men add soneos , lines improvised between the choruses, over a septet directed by its bongo player Frank Oropesa Fernández . posts.title: Daily Discovery: Filimon Bekele & The Ahadu Band – Gamaye
posts.description: Filimon Bekele ranks among the star voices of Tigrigna pop, a singer who writes, produces and programs his own records. In 2013 he was a local favourite around Adigrat, the highland town in northern Tigray close to the Eritrean border. That year Sheba Sound , the UK-based label that has spent more than a decade recording musicians across rural Ethiopia, carried its mobile rig into an open stone farmhouse near the town to record him with his group, The Ahadu Band . On “Gamaye”, the lead single from the label’s new album Kebero , Filimon sings and plays krar , the Ethiopian lyre, run through a small guitar amp. His voice carries a rasp over tight rhythmic krar lines, while a bandmate holds the low end on electric bass. The neighbourhood supplies the rest of the rhythm section: people from around Adigrat beat the kebero , the laced-hide barrel drums that give the album its title, with women wrapped in white netela shawls singing along at the microphones.
